name: Maine
summary: Maine’s State Police page describes recognition of another state’s resident permit when that state recognizes Maine resident permits. This is a recognition question, separate from eligibility for permitless carry.
questions: Resident vs nonresident permit; reciprocal recognition; separate permitless eligibility and location exceptions.

name: New Hampshire
summary: RSA Chapter 159 addresses pistol and revolver definitions, possession restrictions and licensing. Section 159:6 distinguishes availability of a license from unlicensed carry by a person who is not otherwise prohibited. The page includes provisions with different effective dates.
questions: Eligibility, licensing versus carry, vehicle rules, prohibited places and federal overlays.

name: Massachusetts
summary: Massachusetts publishes a research guide linking firearms statutes, licensing resources and related materials. Use it to locate the current rules for the particular firearm and travel purpose; this entry does not establish an exemption.
questions: Current licensing and nonresident provisions, definitions, transport exemptions, restrictions and effective changes.

name: Rhode Island
summary: Rhode Island’s Attorney General explains carry permitting and identifies exceptions in its 2022 guidance. A through-travel exception and permission to carry at a destination are different questions; later changes still need checking.
questions: Distinguish licensing authorities, carry from through-travel exceptions, and later amendments to older guidance.

name: Connecticut
summary: Connecticut’s DESPP page explains state pistol permits and the application process. A permit application, a permit issued by another state and a Connecticut permit are different documents; this reference does not determine recognition or eligibility.
questions: Nonresident licensing, permit scope, current equipment/location restrictions and transport law.

name: New York
summary: New York’s official FAQ covers concealed-carry licensing and related restrictions. Application eligibility is a different question from recognition of an existing permit. Specific locations and current court orders need separate review.
questions: Nonresident application versus permit recognition; NYC distinctions; sensitive places and current litigation/orders.

name: New Jersey
summary: New Jersey provides out-of-state application instructions and separate transportation guidance. These resources address different activities. We have not completed a current-law transport or carry analysis.
questions: Obtain current statutes and orders; the transport guidance is older. Examine authorized purposes, deviations, equipment restrictions and carry/transport distinction.

name: Delaware
summary: Delaware’s Department of Justice provides concealed-carry application and recognition resources. Check the current recognition information and its conditions for your permit and residence before drawing a conclusion.
questions: Current recognition list, residency, temporary recognition, locations and equipment restrictions.

name: Maryland
summary: Maryland State Police explains the Wear & Carry application process and warns that submitting an application does not authorize carrying. The permit page must be read alongside statutory exceptions and location restrictions.
questions: Read Criminal Law 4-203 exceptions alongside permit guidance; compare location rules with current orders and definitions.

name: Virginia
summary: Virginia State Police maintains recognition guidance and links to selected firearms statutes. Full-page retrieval was unavailable during this research pass, so no recognition conditions have been verified here.
questions: Exact recognition prerequisites, identification, age, disqualification, local/location restrictions and transport exceptions. Recognition page discovered via official search result; direct retrieval failed during this pass, so full-page verification remains open.

name: North Carolina
summary: North Carolina G.S. 14-415.24 addresses recognition of a valid concealed-handgun permit or license issued by another state. Recognition alone does not establish that carrying at a particular place or in particular circumstances is lawful.
questions: Recognition does not resolve prohibited places, disclosure requirements or other carry conditions.

name: South Carolina
summary: SLED’s guidance explains South Carolina’s 2024 constitutional-carry legislation. Permitless eligibility, benefits of a permit and prohibited places remain separate questions, and later changes need checking.
questions: Separate permitless eligibility from permit benefits, location restrictions and current amendments; guidance originated in 2024.

name: Georgia
summary: Georgia’s Department of Public Safety publishes firearm-permit reciprocity information. Recognition in a destination state depends on that state’s requirements; the page is not a general authorization for a specific trip.
questions: Lawful-weapons-carrier definition, nonresident eligibility, location restrictions and current statutory exceptions.

name: Florida
summary: Florida’s licensing agency provides reciprocity information and references eligibility conditions. Permit recognition, permitless eligibility and restrictions on where or how to carry require separate review.
questions: Separate recognition, permitless eligibility, open/concealed carry and prohibited places; check current statutes/court orders rather than the scraper's 2023 links.
